summary: LLM inference costs are dominated by token volume, and the same workload can vary 16x in cost depending on model choice alone. Combining prompt caching (up to 90% off cached tokens), semantic response caching (up to 68-73% API call reduction), model routing, and retrieval/context trimming typically cuts total spend by 50-80% while also reducing latency. Fixing retrieval and context bloat usually delivers the biggest wins for the least effort before any wording changes.

techniques.name: Prompt Caching (prefix/KV caching)
techniques.description: Reuses the computed key-value tensors behind a repeated static prompt prefix (system instructions, few-shot examples, large context) so only the dynamic suffix is reprocessed and billed. Cache reads are heavily discounted versus fresh input tokens.
techniques.savings: up to 90% off cached (static-prefix) tokens; ~50-80% on prompt-heavy workloads
techniques.example: Place your fixed system prompt and few-shot examples at the very start of every request so providers like Anthropic (cache_control) and OpenAI automatically bill the repeated prefix at the discounted cache-read rate.

techniques.name: Semantic Response Caching
techniques.description: Stores full LLM responses keyed by an embedding of the request so semantically similar (not just identical) queries return a cached answer without an API call. Ideal for FAQ-style or high-repetition traffic.
techniques.savings: API call reduction up to 68.8%; ~73% cost reduction in high-repetition workloads
techniques.example: Use Redis LangCache or GPTCache to embed incoming questions and return a stored answer when cosine similarity exceeds a threshold (e.g. 0.95), skipping the LLM entirely for near-duplicate queries.

techniques.name: Model Routing / Tiered Model Selection
techniques.description: Routes each request to the cheapest model capable of handling it, sending simple tasks to budget-tier models and only escalating hard tasks to premium models. A classifier or heuristic decides the tier.
techniques.savings: 50-80% depending on traffic mix; up to 16x on tasks movable to budget tiers
techniques.example: Use LiteLLM or an OpenRouter-style router to send classification and extraction tasks to a $0.15/$0.60 budget model and reserve GPT-class models only for complex reasoning.

techniques.name: Fix Retrieval Before Prompt Wording
techniques.description: Tightens RAG retrieval (better chunking, reranking, lower top-k, deduplication) so you pass only the most relevant context instead of stuffing large documents. Reduces input tokens more than any prompt rephrasing.
techniques.example: Add a reranker and cut top-k from 20 chunks to the 4 most relevant, eliminating thousands of wasted context tokens per query.

techniques.name: Prompt Compression / Trimming
techniques.description: Removes redundant instructions, verbose boilerplate, and low-value tokens from prompts, or uses compression models (e.g. LLMLingua) to shrink context while preserving meaning.
techniques.example: Run LLMLingua over long retrieved context to compress it 3-5x before sending, keeping salient tokens and dropping filler.

techniques.name: Output Token Control (max_tokens + concise instructions)
techniques.description: Caps response length and instructs the model to answer concisely or in structured formats, since output tokens are often priced several times higher than input tokens.
techniques.example: Set max_tokens to a realistic ceiling and add 'Respond in under 100 words as a JSON object' to prevent rambling, expensive completions.

techniques.name: Request Batching
techniques.description: Groups multiple independent tasks into a single API call or uses provider async batch APIs that offer large discounts for non-real-time workloads.
techniques.savings: up to 50% via batch-API discounts; reduced per-call overhead
techniques.example: Submit overnight bulk classification jobs through OpenAI's Batch API to receive roughly 50% off standard token pricing.

techniques.name: Streaming + Early Stopping
techniques.description: Streams tokens and halts generation once the needed content (e.g. a closing JSON brace or stop sequence) is produced, avoiding paying for trailing tokens and improving perceived latency.
techniques.savings: 5-20% on output tokens; major latency improvement
techniques.example: Define a stop sequence like '```' or '}' so generation ends as soon as the structured answer is complete.

techniques.name: Structured Outputs / Function Calling
techniques.description: Requests JSON or schema-constrained outputs so the model emits only required fields instead of verbose prose, reducing output tokens and eliminating costly re-prompts for malformed responses.
techniques.savings: 15-40% on output tokens plus fewer retries
techniques.example: Use OpenAI structured outputs with a strict JSON schema to get exactly the five fields you need and nothing more.

tools.name: Redis LangCache / Redis Semantic Cache
tools.description: Managed semantic caching layer that stores and retrieves LLM responses by embedding similarity, reporting up to 73% cost reduction in high-repetition workloads.
tools.pricing_paid: Redis Cloud usage-based tiers; LangCache managed service priced by usage

tools.name: GPTCache
tools.description: Open-source semantic cache for LLMs that stores responses and serves cached answers for similar queries, integrating with LangChain and major providers.
tools.pricing_paid: Free (open source); self-hosted infra costs only

tools.name: LiteLLM
tools.description: Unified proxy/SDK for 100+ LLM providers with built-in model routing, fallback, caching, rate limiting, and cost tracking via a single OpenAI-compatible API.
tools.pricing_paid: Free open-source; LiteLLM Enterprise from ~$250/mo for added governance features

tools.name: Helicone
tools.description: LLM observability and gateway platform providing request logging, cost analytics, caching, and prompt management through a drop-in proxy.
tools.pricing_paid: Paid plans from ~$20/user/mo with higher-volume and enterprise tiers

tools.name: LangChain
tools.description: Framework for building LLM apps with built-in caching (in-memory, Redis, SQLite, semantic), retrieval, and routing abstractions.
tools.pricing_paid: Free open source; LangSmith observability from ~$39/user/mo

tools.name: LLMLingua
tools.description: Microsoft open-source prompt compression library that shrinks prompts and context up to 20x while preserving task performance.

tools.name: OpenRouter
tools.description: Unified API and marketplace that routes requests across many model providers with automatic fallback and price/performance-based routing.
tools.pricing_paid: Pay-as-you-go pass-through pricing plus a small platform fee

tools.name: Portkey
tools.description: AI gateway offering semantic caching, routing, retries, load balancing, and observability across multiple LLM providers.
tools.pricing_paid: Paid plans from ~$49/mo with enterprise tiers

quick_wins: Enable prompt caching by moving all static system prompts and few-shot examples to the start of every request to capture up to 90% off repeated-prefix tokens.
Add a semantic response cache (Redis LangCache or GPTCache) in front of FAQ and high-repetition traffic to cut API calls by up to ~68%.
Route simple tasks to a budget-tier model via LiteLLM or OpenRouter and reserve premium models for complex reasoning only.
Set max_tokens ceilings and instruct concise/structured (JSON) outputs to slash expensive output-token spend.
Tighten RAG retrieval: lower top-k, add a reranker, and deduplicate chunks to stop stuffing wasted context tokens.
